parameters.content:
## 3. Apply, Merge & Respond

• Apply Mapping & Merge supports five strategies: concat / left / right / inner / outer
• Uses a business key (joinKey) when provided
• Full audit report (confidence, unmatched fields, applied transforms)
• Consistent success / error envelope returned to the caller

## 2. AI Mapping + Rule Generation

• HTTP Request calls any LLM / mapping service (default = httpbin mock)
• Parse node normalises the response and falls back to a strong heuristic when the AI returns nothing useful
• Supports hints + targetSchema
• Generates executable transform rules (rename, cast, concat, split, date, default …)

## 1. Intake & Validation

• Webhook receives datasetA + datasetB + options
• Code node builds field profiles (types, nulls, examples)
• Early IF branch returns a clean 400 if payload is invalid

## AI-Powered Data Mapping Engine (v2)

Receives two incompatible datasets, uses an AI (or heuristic) mapping step to infer field correspondences, generates executable transformation rules, applies them, and returns a **unified merged dataset** together with a full audit report.

### Request body (POST /webhook/ai-data-map)
```json
{
  "datasetA": [ { ... }, ... ],
  "datasetB": [ { ... }, ... ],
  "hints": { "email_address": "email" },          // optional
  "targetSchema": ["id", "email", "full_name"], // optional
  "mergeStrategy": "left",                       // concat | left | right | inner | outer
  "joinKey": "id",                               // used when strategy ≠ concat
  "minConfidence": 0.55,
  "keepUnmapped": false,
  "simulateStatus": 200                          // optional – forces httpbin status for testing
}
```

### Response envelope
```json
{
  "status": "mapped" | "error",
  "requestId": "...",
  "stats": { ... },
  "data": [ ... ],          // the merged rows
  "report": { ... }         // full mapping audit
}
```

### Nodes (1-line each)
1. Webhook – receives the two datasets + options
2. Code – Validate & Profile – schema profiling + config normalisation
3. IF – Valid? – early exit on bad payload
4. Wait – Pre AI
5. HTTP Request – AI Mapping API (or mock)
6. Code – Parse AI Mappings – normalises AI answer + heuristic fallback
7. IF – AI OK?
8. Code – Generate Transform Rules
9. Code – Apply Mapping & Merge – real join strategies
10. Code – Build Mapping Report
11. Code – Finalize Output
12. Respond to Webhook
13. Error path → structured error response

**Tip for beginners**: Record a short YouTube walkthrough of the request/response and paste the link in a sticky note using the official format.
